title: hello-expert — a self-teaching domain expert on the learning fabric (target: cli)

beats.label: Open the starter README
beats.cue: “An agent that becomes a verifiable expert in a field and keeps getting better on its own.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed crewhaus.yaml stays untouched.

beats.label: Load the keys
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env — this one wants a Thredz key, an Anthropic key, and search.

groups.title: Beat 1 · The spec: two knobs and a domain

beats.label: State the premise
beats.cue: “Two knobs do all the work.” The old 150-line mechanism prompt now ships with CrewHaus.

beats.label: Document the run in the header
beats.cue: The header carries its own recipe — and the three commands to try first.

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape
beats.cue: target: cli — the interactive half of the starter; the daemon shape comes later.

beats.label: Give it long-term memory
beats.cue: “thredz: true ≡ api_key: $THREDZ_API_KEY — THE one argument.” The wiki is the memory.

beats.label: Add the learning block
beats.cue: Domain, curriculum, source allowlist, exam — four lines register the whole learning-loop skill.

beats.label: One paragraph of identity
beats.cue: Numbers with units, SCA standards over blogs — or say you're unsure. That's the persona.

beats.label: Add the researcher sub-agent
beats.cue: One narrow question in, 2–4 verbatim cited snippets out, under 180 words. No synthesis.

beats.label: Grant the builtin tools
beats.cue: The wiki_* tools aren't listed — thredz: registers them under their bare names.

beats.label: Wire ratings into the flywheel
beats.cue: Stars on answers, autoDistill on — ratings fold into a versioned dataset at teardown.

beats.label: Pre-allow recall and research
beats.cue: Recall and research friction-free; wiki writes allowed but audited; run_exam pre-allowed.

beats.label: Let it curate its own plan
beats.cue: It may edit its own curriculum, exam and field notes — Markdown and JSONL, nothing else.

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “lint: clean — no findings.” Parse, the IR passes, and the scope audit — nothing emitted.

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: The spec is sugar; this JSON is what the compiler actually sees. Too long for a terminal — send it to the scratch dir.

verify.note: the whole lowered IR for target cli, redirected so the next beat can open it (a pipe into head would swallow the exit code)

beats.label: Read the IR
beats.cue: `thredz: true` lowered into a real MCP server — mcp_servers.thredz: npx -y thredz-mcp, THREDZ_API_KEY as an env ref, visibility private as a literal.

beats.label: Emit the bundle
beats.cue: Two files out — the agent and its README — and the spec registers as hello-expert@v1.

verify.note: emits the bundle without the boot check; registers hello-expert@v1 into gitignored .crewhaus/specs

beats.label: Open the emitted agent
beats.cue: connectThredz, wireMemory, createExamRunner — the learning fabric, wired at boot.

beats.label: Boot it with the key stripped
beats.cue: Assertion ok, install ok — then the boot halts on the missing THREDZ_API_KEY. Exit 21, by name.
beats.command: env -u THREDZ_API_KEY crewhaus compile live/crewhaus.yaml -o live/dist --check

verify.note: deliberate: --check reports RED (exit 1) because the boot exits 21 on the missing THREDZ_API_KEY — the config gate the README documents. Assertion (11 anchors) and install both pass; `env -u` makes it deterministic whatever the operator's .env holds.

beats.label: Now hand it a key — and watch nothing change
beats.cue: Same command, key supplied: byte-identical RED. --check boots with a scrubbed environment on purpose, so a key in your shell never reaches the bundle. The gate is structural, not credential-dependent.

verify.note: the point of the beat: same RED, same exit 21, same 11 anchors as prove-gate. --check passes only PATH/HOME/proxy/CA through and boots with an empty --env-file, so neither an exported key nor a colocated .env can satisfy an MCP env ref here. A real key is verified by `crewhaus run` in Beat 3 instead.

beats.label: Open the curriculum
beats.cue: The ladder it works down: fundamentals → methods → measurement → frontier.

beats.label: Launch the expert
beats.cue: [needs-key] The wiki is the memory, so boot checks for the Thredz key before anything else.

verify.note: interactive REPL; needs THREDZ_API_KEY + Anthropic credentials

beats.label: Ask it before it knows anything
beats.cue: [needs-key] Empty wiki, honest answer — “I don't know that yet”, and it logs a knowledge gap.
beats.text: What grind and ratio for a balanced V60?

beats.label: Send it to study
beats.cue: [needs-key] Gaps first, then the curriculum. Researchers fan out; cited articles land in the wiki.

verify.note: reads the live web — needs a CREWHAUS_SEARCH_* provider as well

beats.label: Ask the same question again
beats.cue: [needs-key] Same question, answered from memory this time — with slug citations.
beats.text: What grind and ratio for a balanced V60?

beats.label: Open the competency exam
beats.cue: Gold Q&A: Golden Cup extraction yield, TDS, and diagnosing a sour cup.

beats.label: Open the exam rubric
beats.cue: One llm_judge — factual_correctness and grounded_not_bluffed, passing score 4.

beats.label: Sit the exam
beats.cue: [needs-key] run_exam grades in-process — no Bash, no shell-out — and every failure becomes a gap.

verify.note: runs eval/dataset.jsonl through eval/graders.yaml in fresh sessions; needs credentials

beats.label: Exit the REPL
beats.cue: [needs-key] “exit” returns to the shell.

groups.title: One more thing · It studies while you sleep

beats.label: Open the daemon spec
beats.cue: Same domain, same skill, target: channel — plus a heartbeat every 6h.

beats.label: Open the heartbeat doc
beats.cue: The built-in rotation: gaps first, otherwise roughly 3 STUDY to 1 REFLECT, bounded per tick.

beats.label: Lint the second shape
beats.cue: Same learning: block, a local wiki instead of Thredz — and it lints clean too.

verify.note: lint: clean — no findings; reads the committed daemon.yaml, never writes it

beats.label: Compile the daemon — and check it
beats.cue: Five files asserted, deps installed, boot gated on its Slack env refs: GREEN, no key in the room.

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (4 anchors); install ok; boot reached its spec env refs gate

beats.label: Run the supervised dev loop
beats.cue: [manual] Recompiles and relaunches on every change; status page on localhost:4173.

verify.note: long-lived supervised daemon — needs Slack app credentials and a human to watch the status page and stop it
